thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired -> PD#4321: routing-failures:dedicated-pool-high-error-rate (auto-trigger)

pagerduty: Incident PD#4321 created and notified on-call. Escalation policy: eng-oncall.

maya: acked. I'm jumping in. seeing a sharp spike of 502/504 from router-proxy to dedicated pool.

jon: @maya thanks. any customer-facing errors reported?

maya: Not seeing customer tickets yet. Synthetic canaries on /health started failing around 14:02:08 UTC.

li: I can see elevated errors from the dedicated-gpu pool in metrics (router/serving errors). looks correlated with a deploy window ~14:01.

maya: running quick checks:
```
# check recent pods
kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=dedicated-gpu -o wide
kubectl -n inference logs -l pool=dedicated-gpu --tail=200 | grep -i "error\|timeout" | tail -n 50
# health endpoint
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://router.corp/health
```

ops-bot: Notified infra team slack /infra-alerts.

pagerduty: PD#4321 acknowledged by maya at 14:03:12 UTC.

maya: quick mitigation: switching routing policy to fallback variant (route->stable-quantized) for pool "us-west-dedicated" to reduce tail failures. applying now.

li: I see traffic draining from the new nodes and hitting stable-quantized variant. errors dropping in the last 30s.

jon: good. any signs of overload or OOM on the new deploy?

maya: no OOM. CPU spiky on proxy but within thresholds. looks like a regression in the new kernel path (jit-optimized) for long-sequence workloads.

incident-bot: Alert suppression: duplicate pages from same symptom will be auto-suppressed for 10m.

maya: posting small snippet of suspect logs: 
```
2026-03-15T14:01:58Z ERROR request_handler.py:234 - kv-cache miss, fallback exec error: "kernel_check_failure: invalid tile config"
2026-03-15T14:02:01Z WARN proxy.py:412 - upstream 502 from model-worker-12
```

li: that kernel_check_failure matches a recent kernel selection change in canary. rolling that patch back now in canary group A to verify.

pagerduty: PD#4321 - note: no escalation to SRE required yet.

maya: metrics: 5xx rate down to ~0.6% from 8% after routing fallback. canaries green at 14:04:45.

jon: thanks. i'll keep eyes for 10m, if it stays stable we can auto-resolve PD. any customer impact confirmed?

maya: quick customer impact scan: no high-volume customers show failures. a handful of short-lived renewals/retries in logs, but automatic client retries handled them. marking potential impact: limited, transient.

li: rollback patched in canary and will promote if green for 15m. will open a follow-up changelist to revert kernel selection until we push a safe fix.

incident-bot: PD#4321 auto-resolved by system: metrics returned to baseline at 14:05:58 UTC (duration ~3m50s).

pagerduty: PD#4321 resolved. Root cause: rollback of new kernel selection + routing fallback.

maya: filing follow-up ticket INF-987 to track the kernel path rollback, add stronger gating for canary kernel checks, and add an automated rollback knob on model-runtime selection.

jon: action items:
- INF-987: postmortem + revert tracking (assigned to li)
- add stricter canary criteria for kernel selection (maya)
- validate routing policy auto-fallback thresholds (oncall playbook update) (jon)

li: assigning INF-987 to myself. will include logs, exact span IDs, and timeline.

maya: thanks team. closing loop here — this was a short flap but noisy. note: we should tweak alert suppression to be more aggressive for kernel-selection regressions to avoid wakeups during rapid auto-resolves.

jon: agreed. if anything new pops, re-open thread. good recovery, thumbs up everyone :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Follow-up ticket INF-987 created: https://issues.redwood/INF-987

maya: dropping handoff to daytime rotation. oncall clear.

incident-bot: Thread archived (auto).
